You are "Rovo Dev" - a friendly and helpful AI agent that can help software developers with their tasks. If asked what LLM you are based on, you may answer with the provider and model family but not the specific version.

You are an expert software development assistant tasked with performing operations against a workspace to resolve a problem statement. You will require multiple iterations to explore the workspace and make changes, using only the available functions.

You will be given access to the files in the workspace and a shell (bash or powershell, depending on the platform) to execute commands.

Guidelines:
- Work exclusively within the provided workspace. Do not attempt to access or modify files outside the workspace. Bash or powershell commands will automatically be executed in the workspace directory, so there is no need to change directories. DO NOT run commands like `cd /workspace && ...` - you are already in the correct directory.
- After receiving tool results, carefully reflect on their quality and determine optimal next steps before proceeding. Use your thinking to plan and iterate based on this new information, and then take the best next action.
- Speed up your solution by testing only the relevant parts of the code base. You do not need to fix issues and failures that are unrelated to the problem statement or your changes.
- If you create any temporary new files, scripts, or helper files for iteration, clean up these files by removing them at the end of the task. All temporary files created for testing purposes should be named with a prefix of "tmp_rovodev_"
- Please write a high quality, general purpose solution. Implement a solution that works correctly for all valid inputs, not just the test cases. Do not hard-code values or create solutions that only work for specific test inputs. Instead, implement the actual logic that solves the problem generally.
- Focus on understanding the problem requirements and implementing the correct algorithm. Tests are there to verify correctness, not to define the solution. Provide a principled implementation that follows best practices and software design principles.
- For maximum efficiency, whenever you need to perform multiple independent operations, invoke all relevant tools simultaneously rather than sequentially.
- Do not use bash/powershell commands to perform actions that can be completed with the other provided functions.
- Resolve the provided task as efficiently as possible. Make the most out of each iteration by making simultaneous tool calls as described above and by focusing on targetted testing.

Explanation of available tools:
- open_files: Opens a set of files in the workspace. Large files will be shown in a "collapsed" state, where the bodies of functions and methods are hidden. Smaller files will be shown in full.
- expand_code_chunks: Shown the content of a single file with specified symbols or line ranges expanded. This function shows the exact same output as open_files for smaller files. For large files, it shows the same output as open_files but with the specified symbols or line ranges expanded in the collapsed view. DO NOT call open_files and expand_code_chunks unnecessarily on the same file if you have already viewed the expanded content.
- grep: Searches for a pattern in the content of files in the workspace.
- find_and_replace_code, create_file, delete_file: These functions enable you to modify the codebase. Use them instead of shell equivalents, unless otherwise instructed.
- bash/powershell: Executes a shell command in the workspace directory. Commands will be executed at the root of the workspace by default, so there is no need to change directories.
- MCP server tools: You may have access to additional tools via MCP servers, accessible via mcp__*__get_tool_schema and mcp__*__invoke_tool functions. These tools provide specialized functionality that may help you gather context and complete your task. Before calling mcp__*__invoke_tool, ALWAYS first call mcp__*__get_tool_schema to get important information about the tools being called.

Tool results and user messages may include <system-reminder> tags. <system-reminder> tags contain useful information and reminders. They are automatically added by the system, and bear no direct relation to the specific tool results or user messages in which they appear.

Important:
- Aim to solve tasks in a "token-efficient" manner. This can be done by calling tools simultaneously, and avoiding calling expand_code_chunks and open_files on a file that has already been opened and expanded - you can just inspect the content of the file in the previous tool output.
- You will be provided with the number of iterations you have consumed at each step. As a guide, here are the number of iterations you should expect to consume for different types of tasks:
    - Simple tasks (e.g. explanation request, specific localized change that doesn't require tests): ~10 iterations or fewer.
    - Medium tasks (e.g. implementing a new feature, fixing a bug that requires some investigation): ~20 iterations.
    - Complex tasks (e.g. refactoring, fixing difficult bugs, implementing complex features): ~30 iterations. Never use more than 30 iterations for a single request from the user.
    - Minor follow-up tasks (e.g., adjustments to your initial solution): ~10 iterations.
- Based on the provided issue or request, aim to resolve the task in an appropriate number of iterations, but do not compromise on quality or end early just to save iterations. If you need more iterations than expected, that's okay.

You are currently in interactive mode. You can ask questions and additional inputs from the user when needed.
But before you do that, you should use the tools available to try getting the information you need by yourself.

Include a simple natural language description of your status before each logical group of actions. Make this feel like a natural part of the conversation, not a separate status update.

Use Markdown **only where semantically correct** (e.g., `inline code`, ```code fences```, lists, tables).
When using markdown in assistant messages, use backticks to format file, directory, function, and class names. Use ( and ) for inline math, [ and ] for block math.

When you respond to the user, always end your message with a question for what to do next, ideally with a few sensible options.

## Important: Markdown File Creation Guidance

Do NOT create `.md` files unless explicitly requested by the user. This applies when:
- Documenting plans or decisions (stream to console instead)
- Creating notes or analysis (provide directly in response)
- Summarizing work (include in response)

Only create `.md` files when explicitly asked by the user.
Avoid duplicating content across console output and `.md` files.

# Arkan Development Guide

## Project Overview

**Arkan** is a sophisticated AI-powered platform for writing and document generation, built for academics, professionals, and students. It combines cutting-edge AI technology with intuitive user experience to democratize access to professional-grade writing tools.

### Technology Stack
- **Frontend**: Next.js 15 with React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- **AI Engine**: Google Genkit with Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite model  
- **Backend**: Firebase (Auth, Firestore, Storage, Functions)
- **UI Framework**: Radix UI components with shadcn/ui
- **State Management**: Zustand + React Query (TanStack)
- **Testing**: Jest with React Testing Library
- **Build Tools**: Turbopack, ESLint, TypeScript

## Development Environment Setup

### Prerequisites
- Node.js 18+
- npm or yarn
- Firebase CLI
- Git

### Getting Started
```bash
# Install dependencies
npm install

# Setup local database
npm run setup-agent-db

# Start development server with Turbopack
npm run dev

# Start Genkit AI development server (separate terminal)
npm run genkit:dev

# Run tests
```

### Firebase Setup

A comprehensive suite of tools for migrating static Genkit flows to dynamic configuration-driven flows.

## 📚 Table of Contents

- [Overview](#overview)

- [Migration Workflow](#migration-workflow)
- [Reports & Output](#reports--output)

## Overview

These scripts automate the migration process from static flows to dynamic flows, including analysis, extraction, generation, testing, benchmarking, and rollback capabilities.

## Scripts

### 1. `analyze-flows.ts`

Analyzes all existing flows and generates a comprehensive migration report.

```bash
npm run analyze-flows
# or
tsx scripts/migration/analyze-flows.ts
```

**Outputs:**
- Flow complexity breakdown (simple/medium/complex)
- Category distribution
- Migration time estimates
- Dependency analysis
- `migration-analysis-report.json`

### 2. `extract-prompts.ts`

Extracts prompts from flow source code and saves them as reusable prompt configurations.

```bash
# Extract from all flows
npm run extract-prompts

# Extract from specific flow
tsx scripts/migration/extract-prompts.ts generate-text
```

**Features:**
- Automatic prompt detection
- Variable extraction
- Firestore persistence
- Categorization

### 3. `create-flow-configs.ts`

Generates dynamic flow configurations from static flow source code.

```bash
# Generate all configs (save to DB)
npm run create-flow-configs

# Dry run (no DB save)
tsx scripts/migration/create-flow-configs.ts --dry-run

# Generate specific flow
tsx scripts/migration/create-flow-configs.ts generate-text
```

**Outputs:**
- Flow configuration JSON files in `migration-configs/`
- Firestore documents (if not dry-run)
- Summary report

### 4. `migrate-flows.ts`

Orchestrates the complete migration process: analyze → generate → validate → save.

```bash
# Migrate all flows (all phases)
npm run migrate-flows

# Migrate specific phase
tsx scripts/migration/migrate-flows.ts --phase=1

# Migrate specific flows
tsx scripts/migration/migrate-flows.ts --flows=generate-text,paraphrase-text
```

**Migration Phases:**
1. **Simple Text Generation** (15 flows)
2. **Analysis Tools** (8 flows)
3. **Complex Document Generation** (14 flows)
4. **Academic & Research** (9 flows)
5. **Special & RAG-Enhanced** (8 flows)

**Outputs:**
- Per-phase reports in `migration-reports/`
- Backups in `migration-backups/`
- Final summary report

### 5. `compare-outputs.ts`

Compares outputs from static vs dynamic flows to validate migration accuracy.

```bash
# Compare specific flow (3 runs per test)
npm run compare-outputs generate-text

# More runs for better accuracy
tsx scripts/migration/compare-outputs.ts generate-text --runs=10
```

**Metrics:**
- Output similarity percentage
- Identical output detection
- Difference analysis
- Recommendation (PASS/REVIEW/FAIL)

**Outputs:**
- Comparison reports in `migration-reports/comparisons/`

### 6. `benchmark-flow.ts`

Measures performance characteristics of static vs dynamic flows.

```bash
# Benchmark with 100 iterations
npm run benchmark-flow generate-text

# More iterations for accuracy
tsx scripts/migration/benchmark-flow.ts generate-text --iterations=500
```

**Metrics:**
- Execution time (mean, median, P95, P99)
- Memory usage
- Throughput (requests/sec)
- Standard deviation
- Performance comparison

**Outputs:**
- Benchmark reports in `migration-reports/benchmarks/`

### 7. `rollback-migration.ts`

Safely rollback migrations with backup preservation.

```bash
# List all migrated flows
tsx scripts/migration/rollback-migration.ts --list

# Soft rollback (disable, keep config)
tsx scripts/migration/rollback-migration.ts generate-text

# Hard rollback (delete config)
tsx scripts/migration/rollback-migration.ts generate-text --hard

# Rollback all flows
tsx scripts/migration/rollback-migration.ts --hard

# Restore from backup
tsx scripts/migration/rollback-migration.ts --restore=migration-backups/generate-text_1234567890.json
```

**Rollback Types:**
- **Soft**: Disables flow but keeps configuration for analysis
- **Hard**: Completely removes configuration (with backup)

**Outputs:**
- Rollback reports in `migration-reports/rollbacks/`
- Backups in `migration-backups/rollbacks/` or `migration-backups/hard-rollbacks/`

## Usage Guide

### Initial Analysis

Before starting migration, run analysis to understand the scope:

```bash
npm run analyze-flows
```

Review `migration-analysis-report.json` to understand:
- Total flows and complexity breakdown
- Estimated migration time
- Dependencies and warnings

### Phase-by-Phase Migration

Follow the recommended migration order:

```bash
# Phase 1: Simple flows
tsx scripts/migration/migrate-flows.ts --phase=1

# Validate Phase 1
tsx scripts/migration/compare-outputs.ts generate-text --runs=5
tsx scripts/migration/benchmark-flow.ts generate-text --iterations=100

# Phase 2: Analysis flows
tsx scripts/migration/migrate-flows.ts --phase=2

# Continue for phases 3, 4, 5...
```

### Testing Individual Flows

After migrating a flow, thoroughly test it:

```bash
FLOW_NAME="generate-text"

# 1. Compare outputs
tsx scripts/migration/compare-outputs.ts $FLOW_NAME --runs=10

# 2. Benchmark performance
tsx scripts/migration/benchmark-flow.ts $FLOW_NAME --iterations=200

# 3. If issues found, rollback
tsx scripts/migration/rollback-migration.ts $FLOW_NAME
```

### Full Migration Workflow

Complete end-to-end migration:

```bash
# 1. Analysis
npm run analyze-flows

# 2. Extract prompts (optional, for reusability)
npm run extract-prompts

# 3. Generate configs (dry-run first)
tsx scripts/migration/create-flow-configs.ts --dry-run

# 4. Review generated configs in migration-configs/
# 5. Generate and save to DB
npm run create-flow-configs

# 6. Run full migration
npm run migrate-flows

# 7. Review reports in migration-reports/
```

## Migration Workflow

### Recommended Process

1. **Pre-Migration**
   - Run analysis
   - Review complexity breakdown
   - Plan phases based on complexity
   - Ensure database backups

2. **Migration Execution**
   - Start with simple flows (Phase 1)
   - Migrate phase by phase
   - Test each phase before proceeding
   - Monitor performance metrics

3. **Validation**
   - Compare outputs for critical flows
   - Benchmark performance
   - Manual testing of complex flows
   - User acceptance testing

4. **Rollback Planning**
   - Keep all backups
   - Document any issues
   - Have rollback procedures ready
   - Test rollback process

### Quality Gates

Before proceeding to next phase:

- ✅ All migrations successful
- ✅ Output comparison > 90% similarity
- ✅ Performance overhead < 20%
- ✅ Manual testing passed
- ✅ No critical errors in logs

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

**Issue**: Flow config generation fails
```bash
# Check if flow file exists
ls -la src/ai/flows/flow-name.ts

# Try dry-run first
tsx scripts/migration/create-flow-configs.ts flow-name --dry-run
```

**Issue**: Low output similarity
```bash
# Run more comparison tests
tsx scripts/migration/compare-outputs.ts flow-name --runs=20

# Check for randomness in outputs
# Review flow implementation for non-deterministic behavior
```

**Issue**: Poor performance
```bash
# Run detailed benchmark
tsx scripts/migration/benchmark-flow.ts flow-name --iterations=500

# Check memory leaks
node --expose-gc scripts/migration/benchmark-flow.ts flow-name
```

**Issue**: Migration fails mid-process
```bash
# Check last successful flow in reports
cat migration-reports/phase-X-report.json

# Resume from specific flows
tsx scripts/migration/migrate-flows.ts --flows=remaining-flow-1,remaining-flow-2
```

## Best Practices

1. **Always run analysis first** to understand scope
2. **Use dry-run mode** before saving to database
3. **Test incrementally** - don't migrate all at once
4. **Keep backups** - never delete backup files
5. **Monitor performance** throughout migration
6. **Document issues** found during migration
7. **Have rollback plan** ready before starting
8. **Validate critical flows** manually after migration

**Version**: 1.0

**Target Audience**: End Users, Content Creators

---

## 📚 Table of Contents

1. [Introduction](#introduction)
2. [Getting Started](#getting-started)
3. [Using Dynamic Flows](#using-dynamic-flows)

## Introduction

### What are Dynamic Flows?

Dynamic Flows is a powerful system that allows you to execute AI-powered workflows without writing code. Each flow is a pre-configured process that takes your input and produces intelligent output.

### Key Benefits

- ✅ **No Coding Required** - Simple interface for everyone
- ✅ **Instant Results** - Fast AI-powered processing
- ✅ **54 Available Flows** - Covering text, analysis, documents, and more
- ✅ **Reliable** - Tested and production-ready
- ✅ **Flexible** - Configurable inputs and outputs

---

## Getting Started

### Accessing the System

1. **Login** to your account at the application URL
2. **Navigate** to the flows section
3. **Select** a flow that matches your needs
4. **Provide** required inputs
5. **Execute** and get results

### Your First Flow

Let's try a simple text generation flow:

1. Navigate to "Writing Tools" → "Generate Text"
2. Enter your prompt: `"Write a short paragraph about AI"`
3. Click "Generate"
4. Review your results

That's it! You've executed your first dynamic flow.

---

## Using Dynamic Flows

### Understanding Flow Types

Flows are organized into categories:

#### Text Transformation (9 flows)
- Generate, paraphrase, summarize, translate text
- Humanize AI content, manipulate text
- Convert to markdown

#### Analysis Tools (8 flows)
- Grammar checking, bias detection
- Fact checking, plagiarism detection
- AI content detection

#### Document Generation (10 flows)
- Write documents, reports, chapters
- Create presentations, technical specs
- Generate project documentation

#### Education (7 flows)
- Create quizzes, lesson plans
- Generate lecture content
- Solve assignments

#### Academic (11 flows)
- Literature reviews, research assistance
- Paper quality checking, proofreading
- Project blueprints

#### Development (4 flows)
- Generate UI descriptions
- Create technical specifications
- Project documentation

#### Multimodal (3 flows)
- Image to text conversion
- Text to speech metadata
- Image generation specs

#### RAG-Enhanced (2 flows)
- Context-aware report sections
- Context-aware chapter generation

### Flow Execution

#### Basic Steps

1. **Select Flow**
   - Browse by category
   - Search by name
   - Filter by tags

2. **Configure Input**
   - Fill required fields (marked with *)
   - Optionally fill additional fields
   - Review input guidelines

3. **Execute**
   - Click "Execute" or "Generate"
   - Wait for processing (usually < 30 seconds)
   - View progress indicator

4. **Review Results**
   - Check output quality
   - Copy or download results
   - Re-execute if needed

#### Input Best Practices

✅ **Be Specific** - Clear inputs get better outputs  
✅ **Provide Context** - More context = better results  
✅ **Use Examples** - Show what you want  
✅ **Check Requirements** - Meet field requirements  

#### Understanding Output

Each flow returns specific output types:

- **Text**: Plain text or markdown
- **JSON**: Structured data
- **Object**: Complex structured output

---

## Available Flows

### Text Generation & Transformation

#### generate-text
**Purpose**: Generate text from prompts  
**Input**: Text prompt  
**Output**: Generated text  
**Use Case**: Content creation, ideas, drafts

#### paraphrase-text
**Purpose**: Rewrite text in different styles  
**Input**: Text, style (standard/fluent/formal/creative/simplify)  
**Output**: Paraphrased text  
**Use Case**: Content variation, style adjustment

#### summarize-text
**Purpose**: Create summaries  
**Input**: Text, length (short/medium/long)  
**Output**: Summary  
**Use Case**: Quick understanding, condensing content

#### translate-text
**Purpose**: Translate to other languages  
**Input**: Text, target language  
**Output**: Translated text (markdown preserved)  
**Use Case**: Multilingual content

#### humanize-text
**Purpose**: Make AI text sound human  
**Input**: AI-generated text  
**Output**: Humanized text  
**Use Case**: Natural-sounding content

### Analysis Tools

#### grammar-checker
**Purpose**: Check and correct grammar  
**Input**: Text  
**Output**: Corrected text + issues list  
**Use Case**: Writing quality improvement

#### bias-checker
**Purpose**: Detect bias in text  
**Input**: Text  
**Output**: Bias score, identified biases, recommendations  
**Use Case**: Fair, balanced writing

#### fact-checker
**Purpose**: Verify factual claims  
**Input**: Text with claims  
**Output**: Claims + verification results  
**Use Case**: Accuracy verification

#### plagiarism-checker
**Purpose**: Check originality  
**Input**: Text  
**Output**: Originality score, suspicious phrases  
**Use Case**: Content uniqueness

#### detect-ai-content
**Purpose**: Detect AI-generated content  
**Input**: Text  
**Output**: AI probability, indicators  
**Use Case**: Content authenticity

### Document Generation

#### write-document
**Purpose**: Create comprehensive documents  
**Input**: Title, type, requirements, context  
**Output**: Complete document (markdown)  
**Use Case**: Document creation

#### generate-report-section
**Purpose**: Generate report sections  
**Input**: Section title, type, content requirements  
**Output**: Report section (markdown)  
**Use Case**: Report building

#### generate-chapter-content
**Purpose**: Create book chapters  
**Input**: Chapter title, topics, style  
**Output**: Complete chapter  
**Use Case**: Book writing

### Education

#### generate-quiz
**Purpose**: Create quizzes  
**Input**: Topic, difficulty, question count  
**Output**: Quiz with Q&A  
**Use Case**: Assessment creation

#### generate-session-plan
**Purpose**: Create lesson plans  
**Input**: Subject, duration, grade level, objectives  
**Output**: Detailed session plan  
**Use Case**: Teaching preparation

### Academic

#### ai-researcher
**Purpose**: Research assistance  
**Input**: Research question, field, depth  
**Output**: Research findings and analysis  
**Use Case**: Academic research

#### literature-review-generator
**Purpose**: Generate literature reviews  
**Input**: Topic, sources, approach  
**Output**: Formatted literature review  
**Use Case**: Academic writing

#### academic-paper-quality-checker
**Purpose**: Assess paper quality  
**Input**: Paper text, type, criteria  
**Output**: Quality assessment report  
**Use Case**: Paper improvement

---

## Best Practices

### Getting Better Results

1. **Clear Prompts**
   - Be specific about what you want
   - Provide examples when helpful
   - Include relevant context

2. **Appropriate Flow Selection**
   - Choose the right flow for your task
   - Check input requirements
   - Understand expected output

3. **Iterative Refinement**
   - Review initial results
   - Adjust inputs if needed
   - Re-execute for better results

4. **Context Matters**
   - More context = better output
   - Include relevant details
   - Specify constraints

### Common Mistakes to Avoid

❌ **Vague Inputs** - "Write something" vs. "Write a technical blog post about AI"  
❌ **Wrong Flow** - Using generate-text for analysis tasks  
❌ **Missing Context** - Not providing necessary background  
❌ **Ignoring Requirements** - Not filling required fields  

### Performance Tips

- ✅ Keep inputs concise but complete
- ✅ Use appropriate flow for task
- ✅ Check output immediately
- ✅ Save or copy results promptly

---

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

#### Flow Execution Fails

**Problem**: Flow doesn't execute  
**Solutions**:
- Check all required fields are filled
- Verify input format is correct
- Check internet connection
- Try again after a moment

#### Poor Quality Output

**Problem**: Results don't meet expectations  
**Solutions**:
- Make prompt more specific
- Add more context
- Try different phrasing
- Use a different flow if more appropriate

#### Slow Performance

**Problem**: Flow takes too long  
**Solutions**:
- Check input size (very large inputs take longer)
- Verify system status
- Try during off-peak hours
- Contact support if persistent

#### Unexpected Results

**Problem**: Output is not what expected  
**Solutions**:
- Review input for clarity
- Check if correct flow was selected
- Add examples to input
- Provide more specific requirements

### Error Messages

| Error | Meaning | Solution |
|-------|---------|----------|
| "Invalid input" | Input doesn't meet requirements | Check field requirements |
| "Flow not found" | Selected flow unavailable | Refresh page, try again |
| "Execution timeout" | Flow took too long | Reduce input size, retry |
| "Rate limit exceeded" | Too many requests | Wait a moment, try again |

---

## FAQ

### General Questions

**Q: How many flows are available?**  
A: 54 flows covering various categories.

**Q: Do I need to know coding?**  
A: No, the system is designed for non-technical users.

**Q: How long does execution take?**  
A: Most flows complete in under 30 seconds.

**Q: Can I save my results?**  
A: Yes, you can copy or download results.

**Q: Is my data secure?**  
A: Yes, all data is processed securely and privately.

### Technical Questions

**Q: What AI model is used?**  
A: We use Google's Gemini 2.0 Flash model.

**Q: Can I customize flows?**  
A: Admins can modify flow configurations.

**Q: What input formats are supported?**  
A: Text, JSON, and specific structured formats per flow.

**Q: What output formats are available?**  
A: Text, markdown, JSON, depending on the flow.

**Q: Are there usage limits?**  
A: Limits may apply based on your account type.

### Usage Questions

**Q: Can I use flows for commercial purposes?**  
A: Check your license agreement for commercial use terms.

**Q: How accurate are the results?**  
A: Results are AI-generated and should be reviewed.

**Q: Can I execute multiple flows?**  
A: Yes, you can execute flows sequentially or in parallel.

**Q: How do I report issues?**  
A: Contact support with details about the issue.

---

## Support

### Getting Help

- **Documentation**: Check this guide and admin documentation
- **Support**: Contact support team
- **Community**: Join user community forums
- **Updates**: Check release notes for new features

### Contact Information

- **Support Email**: support@example.com
- **Documentation**: docs.example.com
- **Community Forum**: community.example.com

---

## Appendix

### Glossary

- **Flow**: Pre-configured AI workflow
- **Input**: Data provided to a flow
- **Output**: Results from flow execution
- **Configuration**: Flow settings and parameters
- **RAG**: Retrieval Augmented Generation (context-aware)

### Quick Reference

| Task | Recommended Flow |
|------|------------------|
| Write content | generate-text |
| Rewrite text | paraphrase-text |
| Summarize | summarize-text |
| Translate | translate-text |
| Check grammar | grammar-checker |
| Check facts | fact-checker |
| Create quiz | generate-quiz |
| Research | ai-researcher |
| Write document | write-document |

---

**Version**: 1.0  
**Last Updated**: 2026-01-14  
**Target Audience**: System Administrators, DevOps

---

## 📚 Table of Contents

1. [System Overview](#system-overview)
2. [Architecture](#architecture)
3. [Flow Management](#flow-management)
4. [Configuration](#configuration)
5. [Monitoring](#monitoring)
6. [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
7. [Maintenance](#maintenance)
8. [Security](#security)

---

## System Overview

### What You're Managing

The Dynamic Flows System consists of:
- **54 Flow Configurations** - Database-stored workflows
- **5 Step Types** - Generate, Retrieve, Tool, Condition, Loop
- **Flow Executor** - Core execution engine
- **Configuration Service** - CRUD operations
- **Cache Layer** - Performance optimization

### Key Responsibilities

- ✅ Flow configuration management
- ✅ Performance monitoring
- ✅ User access control
- ✅ System maintenance
- ✅ Backup and recovery

---

## Architecture

### System Components

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  Frontend Layer                  │
│  (Flow Builder UI, User Interface)              │
└────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
┌────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
│                  API Layer                       │
│  (Management APIs, Execution APIs)              │
└────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
┌────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
│                Service Layer                     │
│  (Flow Config Service, Cache, Executor)         │
└────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
┌────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
│                Data Layer                        │
│  (Firestore: flowConfigs, prompts, traces)     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Data Flow

1. User selects flow → 2. API validates input → 3. Service fetches config (cache or DB) → 4. Executor processes steps → 5. Results returned

### File Structure

```
src/
├── ai/
│   ├── flows/               # Original static flows (reference)
│   └── dynamic-flow/
│       ├── step-handlers.ts # Step execution logic
│       └── context-manager.ts
├── services/
│   ├── flow-config-service.ts  # Configuration CRUD
│   └── execution-service.ts
├── lib/
│   ├── models/flow-config.ts   # Type definitions
│   └── cache/flow-config-cache.ts  # Caching layer
└── app/api/
    └── flows/
        └── execute/route.ts    # Execution endpoint

migration-configs/
├── pilot/          # 5 pilot flows
├── phase1/         # 10 simple flows
├── phase2/         # 8 analysis flows
├── phase3/         # 14 complex flows
├── phase4/         # 9 academic flows
└── phase5/         # 8 special flows
```

---

## Flow Management

### Accessing Flow Configurations

#### Via Firestore Console
1. Navigate to Firebase Console
2. Select Firestore Database
3. Open `flowConfigs` collection
4. View/edit configurations

#### Via Admin UI
1. Login as admin
2. Navigate to Admin → Flow Builder
3. Browse or search flows
4. Edit, create, or delete

### Flow Configuration Structure

```json
{
  "name": "flow-name",
  "version": 1,
  "description": "Flow description",
  "category": "category-name",
  "tags": ["tag1", "tag2"],
  "isActive": true,
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": { ... },
    "required": [ ... ]
  },
  "outputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": { ... },
    "required": [ ... ]
  },
  "steps": [
    {
      "id": "step_1",
      "name": "Step Name",
      "type": "generate|retrieve|tool|condition|loop",
      "config": { ... },
      "outputMapping": { ... }
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "createdAt": "ISO-8601",
    "updatedAt": "ISO-8601",
    "sourceFile": "path/to/original"
  }
}
```

### Creating New Flows

#### Method 1: Via Admin UI
1. Navigate to Flow Builder
2. Click "Create New Flow"
3. Fill basic information
4. Add steps
5. Configure each step
6. Set output mapping
7. Validate and save

#### Method 2: Via JSON Import
1. Create JSON configuration file
2. Validate structure
3. Import via Admin UI or API
4. Test execution

#### Method 3: Clone Existing Flow
1. Find similar flow
2. Click "Clone"
3. Modify as needed
4. Save as new flow

### Modifying Flows

**Best Practices**:
- ✅ Test changes in development first
- ✅ Use version control
- ✅ Document changes
- ✅ Backup before major changes
- ✅ Notify users of changes

**Version Management**:
- Increment version number for changes
- Keep old versions for rollback
- Document version changes
- Track who made changes

### Deactivating Flows

To temporarily disable a flow:
1. Open flow configuration
2. Set `isActive: false`
3. Save changes
4. Users will not see the flow

### Deleting Flows

**⚠️ Warning**: Deletion is permanent!

1. Backup configuration first
2. Check for dependencies
3. Notify users if widely used
4. Delete from Firestore
5. Clear from cache
6. Document deletion

---

## Configuration

### Environment Variables

```bash
# Firebase Configuration
NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=...
NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=...
NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=...

# AI Model Configuration
AI_MODEL=gemini-2.0-flash-exp
AI_API_KEY=...

# Cache Configuration
CACHE_TTL=300000  # 5 minutes in ms
CACHE_MAX_SIZE=1000

# Rate Limiting
RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=60
RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR=1000
```

### Cache Configuration

Edit `src/lib/cache/flow-config-cache.ts`:

```typescript
private readonly defaultTTL: number = 5 * 60 * 1000; // Adjust TTL
```

**Cache Management**:
- Clear cache: Call `flowConfigCache.clear()`
- Check stats: Call `flowConfigCache.getStats()`
- Manual cleanup: Call `flowConfigCache.cleanExpired()`

### Database Indexes

Ensure Firestore indexes exist for:
- `flowConfigs`: name, category, isActive, tags
- `executionTraces`: flowName, timestamp
- `prompts`: category, tags, isActive

### Performance Tuning

**Database**:
- Use composite indexes
- Limit query results
- Use pagination
- Cache frequently accessed data

**Execution**:
- Monitor step execution times
- Optimize slow steps
- Use connection pooling
- Implement request queuing

---

## Monitoring

### Key Metrics to Monitor

#### Execution Metrics
- Executions per minute/hour
- Average execution time
- Success vs failure rate
- Error types and frequency

#### Performance Metrics
- API response times
- Database query times
- Cache hit rate
- Memory usage

#### Resource Metrics
- CPU usage
- Memory consumption
- Network bandwidth
- Database connections

### Monitoring Tools

**Firebase Console**:
- Firestore usage
- Function executions
- Authentication activity

**Application Logs**:
- Execution traces
- Error logs
- Performance logs

**Cache Statistics**:
```javascript
const stats = flowConfigCache.getStats();
console.log('Cache size:', stats.size);
console.log('Cached flows:', stats.entries);
```

### Setting Up Alerts

Configure alerts for:
- High error rates (> 5%)
- Slow response times (> 10s)
- High resource usage (> 80%)
- Failed authentications
- Database errors

---

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

#### Flow Execution Failures

**Symptoms**: Flows fail to execute  
**Diagnosis**:
1. Check execution logs
2. Verify configuration validity
3. Test with simple input
4. Check AI model availability

**Solutions**:
- Fix configuration errors
- Validate input schemas
- Check API keys
- Restart services if needed

#### Performance Degradation

**Symptoms**: Slow response times  
**Diagnosis**:
1. Check cache hit rate
2. Review database queries
3. Monitor resource usage
4. Check network latency

**Solutions**:
- Increase cache TTL
- Optimize database queries
- Scale resources
- Enable CDN

#### Cache Issues

**Symptoms**: Stale configurations, memory issues  
**Diagnosis**:
1. Check cache stats
2. Review TTL settings
3. Monitor memory usage

**Solutions**:
- Clear cache
- Adjust TTL
- Implement cache eviction
- Restart application

#### Database Connection Issues

**Symptoms**: Connection timeouts, errors  
**Diagnosis**:
1. Check Firestore status
2. Review connection limits
3. Check authentication

**Solutions**:
- Verify credentials
- Increase connection pool
- Check firewall rules
- Contact Firebase support

### Debug Mode

Enable debug logging:

```typescript
// In flow executor
const DEBUG = process.env.DEBUG_FLOWS === 'true';

if (DEBUG) {
  console.log('Executing step:', step.name);
  console.log('Context:', context.getAll());
}
```

### Log Analysis

**Important logs to check**:
- Execution start/end times
- Step-by-step progress
- Error messages and stack traces
- Input/output data
- Performance metrics

---

## Maintenance

### Regular Tasks

#### Daily
- ✅ Review error logs
- ✅ Check system health
- ✅ Monitor performance metrics

#### Weekly
- ✅ Analyze usage patterns
- ✅ Review slow queries
- ✅ Check disk usage
- ✅ Update documentation

#### Monthly
- ✅ Database cleanup
- ✅ Performance optimization
- ✅ Security audit
- ✅ Backup verification
- ✅ Update dependencies

### Backup Procedures

**Configuration Backup**:
```bash
# Export all flow configs
npm run export:flows

# Backup to secure location
cp migration-configs/*.json /backups/$(date +%Y%m%d)/
```

**Database Backup**:
- Use Firebase automated backups
- Export Firestore data weekly
- Store backups in multiple locations
- Test restore procedures monthly

### Update Procedures

**Updating Flow Configurations**:
1. Backup current configuration
2. Make changes in development
3. Test thoroughly
4. Deploy to staging
5. Validate in staging
6. Deploy to production
7. Monitor for issues

**System Updates**:
1. Review change log
2. Test in development
3. Schedule maintenance window
4. Notify users
5. Deploy updates
6. Verify functionality
7. Monitor post-deployment

---

```javascript
// firestore.rules
rules_version = '2';
service cloud.firestore {
  match /databases/{database}/documents {
    // Flow configurations - read for authenticated, write for admins
    match /flowConfigs/{flowId} {
      allow read: if request.auth != null;
      allow write: if request.auth != null && 
                     get(/databases/$(database)/documents/users/$(request.auth.uid)).data.role == 'admin';

    // Execution traces - authenticated users
    match /executionTraces/{traceId} {
      allow read, write: if request.auth != null;

  }
}
```

# Arkan Development Guide

## Project Overview

**Arkan** is a sophisticated AI-powered platform for writing and document generation, built for academics, professionals, and students. It combines cutting-edge AI technology with intuitive user experience to democratize access to professional-grade writing tools.

### Technology Stack
- **Frontend**: Next.js 15 with React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- **AI Engine**: Google Genkit with Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite model  
- **Backend**: Firebase (Auth, Firestore, Storage, Functions)
- **UI Framework**: Radix UI components with shadcn/ui
- **State Management**: Zustand + React Query (TanStack)
- **Testing**: Jest with React Testing Library
- **Build Tools**: Turbopack, ESLint, TypeScript

## Development Environment Setup

### Prerequisites
- Node.js 18+
- npm or yarn
- Firebase CLI
- Git

### Getting Started
```bash
# Install dependencies
npm install

# Setup local database
npm run setup-agent-db

# Start development server with Turbopack
npm run dev

# Start Genkit AI development server (separate terminal)
npm run genkit:dev

# Run tests
npm test

# Type checking
npm run typecheck
```

### Firebase Setup
```bash
# Start Firebase emulators for local development
firebase emulators:start

# Seed the database with initial data
npm run seed
```

## Architecture & Code Organization

### Directory Structure
```
src/
├── ai/                 # AI flows, schemas, and Genkit configuration
│   ├── flows/          # Individual AI operations (23+ tools)
│   ├── schemas/        # Zod validation schemas
│   └── core/           # Core AI functionality
├── app/                # Next.js App Router pages and API routes
├── components/         # Reusable UI components (organized by domain)
├── hooks/              # Custom React hooks (grouped by functionality)
├── lib/                # Utility libraries and database operations
├── services/           # API service layers and external integrations
└── types/              # TypeScript type definitions
```

### Key Files & Directories

#### AI System
- `src/ai/flows/index.ts` - Barrel exports for all AI flows
- `src/ai/schemas/` - Type-safe validation for AI inputs/outputs
- `src/ai/genkit.ts` - Genkit AI configuration
- `src/ai/core/context.ts` - Context-aware report generation

#### Database & Services
- `src/lib/db/` - SQLite database setup and queries
- `src/services/api/` - Service layer for API calls
- `src/lib/firebase/` - Firebase configuration and utilities

#### UI Components
- `src/components/ui/` - Base UI components (shadcn/ui)
- `src/components/writing-tools/` - Writing tool specific components
- `src/components/shared/` - Shared application components

## Development Best Practices

### Code Style & Conventions

#### File Naming
- Use kebab-case for files and directories
- Use PascalCase for React components
- Use camelCase for functions and variables
- Barrel exports: Always include `index.ts` files for clean imports

#### TypeScript Guidelines
- Enable strict mode (already configured)
- Use type imports where possible: `import type { User } from '@/types'`
- Define schemas with Zod for runtime validation
- Prefer interfaces over type aliases for object shapes

#### Component Patterns
```typescript
// Preferred component structure
interface ComponentProps {
  children?: React.ReactNode;
  className?: string;
}

export function Component({ children, className }: ComponentProps) {
  // Implementation
}
```

#### Custom Hooks Pattern
```typescript
// Business logic separation
export function useFeatureName() {
  const [state, setState] = useState();
  
  // Logic here
  
  return {
    // Return object with clear API
  };
}
```

### AI Flow Development

#### Creating New AI Flows
1. Define input/output schemas in `src/ai/schemas/flows.ts`
2. Create flow file in `src/ai/flows/`
3. Export from `src/ai/flows/index.ts`
4. Add corresponding UI component in `src/components/writing-tools/`

#### AI Flow Template
```typescript
import { ai } from '@/ai/genkit';
import { z } from 'genkit';

const FlowInputSchema = z.object({
  // Define input structure
});

const FlowOutputSchema = z.object({
  // Define output structure
});

export const myAiFlow = ai.defineFlow({
  name: 'myAiFlow',
  inputSchema: FlowInputSchema,
  outputSchema: FlowOutputSchema,
}, async (input) => {
  // Implementation
});
```

### State Management Patterns

#### Zustand Store Structure
```typescript
interface StoreState {
  // State shape
}

interface StoreActions {
  // Action methods
}

export const useStore = create<StoreState & StoreActions>((set, get) => ({
  // Implementation
}));
```

#### React Query Integration
- Use React Query for server state management
- Zustand for client-side UI state only
- Custom hooks to encapsulate query logic

### Database Patterns

#### Firestore Best Practices
- Use subcollections for related data
- Implement proper security rules in `firestore.rules`
- Batch operations for multiple writes
- Use transactions for data consistency

#### SQLite Local Database
- Agent configurations stored locally
- Use prepared statements for queries
- Database schema in `src/lib/db/agent-database.sql`

## UI Development Guidelines

### Component Design System
- Use Radix UI primitives for accessibility
- Extend with Tailwind CSS for styling
- Follow shadcn/ui patterns for consistency
- Support both light/dark themes

### Responsive Design
- Mobile-first approach
- Use Tailwind responsive prefixes
- Test on various screen sizes
- Consider RTL layout for Arabic support

### Internationalization (i18n)
- Support English and Arabic
- Use proper RTL layout techniques
- Font loading for different languages
- Cultural adaptation for date/number formats

## API Development

### Next.js API Routes
- Place in `src/app/api/` directory
- Use TypeScript for type safety
- Implement proper error handling
- Follow RESTful conventions

### Server Actions
- Use for form submissions
- Validate inputs with Zod schemas
- Handle errors gracefully
- Return appropriate status codes

### Firebase Integration
- Use Firebase Admin SDK on server
- Client SDK for frontend operations
- Implement proper authentication checks
- Follow Firebase security best practices

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Testing
- Jest with React Testing Library
- Test components in isolation
- Mock external dependencies
- Focus on user interactions

### Integration Testing
- Test API routes with real database
- Use Firebase emulators for testing
- Test critical user flows
- Performance testing for AI operations

## Performance Optimization

### Frontend Performance
- Use Next.js Image optimization
- Implement code splitting
- Lazy load components where appropriate
- Optimize bundle size with webpack-bundle-analyzer

### AI Operations
- Cache AI responses when appropriate
- Implement request debouncing
- Stream responses for long operations
- Handle rate limiting gracefully

### Database Optimization
- Index frequently queried fields
- Use Firestore compound queries efficiently
- Implement pagination for large datasets
- Cache static data appropriately

## Security Guidelines

### Authentication & Authorization
- Use Firebase Auth for user management
- Implement role-based access control
- Protect sensitive routes with middleware
- Validate user permissions server-side

### Data Protection
- Validate all inputs with Zod schemas
- Sanitize user content before storage
- Implement proper CORS policies
- Use HTTPS in production

### AI Safety
- Implement content filtering
- Rate limit AI operations per user
- Monitor for abuse patterns
- Validate AI outputs before display

## Common Development Patterns

### Error Handling
```typescript
// Consistent error handling pattern
try {
  const result = await apiCall();
  return { success: true, data: result };
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Operation failed:', error);
  return { 
    success: false, 
    error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error' 
  };
}
```

### Loading States
```typescript
// Standard loading pattern
const { data, isLoading, error } = useQuery({
  queryKey: ['resource'],
  queryFn: fetchResource,
});

if (isLoading) return <LoadingSpinner />;
if (error) return <ErrorDisplay error={error} />;
return <DataDisplay data={data} />;
```

### Form Handling
```typescript
// React Hook Form with Zod validation
const form = useForm<FormData>({
  resolver: zodResolver(formSchema),
});

const onSubmit = async (data: FormData) => {
  // Handle form submission
};
```

## Environment Configuration

### Development
- Use Firebase emulators for local development
- Hot reload with Turbopack
- Debug mode for AI operations

### Production
- Firebase Hosting for deployment
- Environment variables for sensitive data
- Monitoring and analytics enabled

## Troubleshooting Common Issues

### AI Flow Issues
- Check Genkit server is running: `npm run genkit:dev`
- Verify API keys in environment variables
- Check input schema validation

### Database Issues
- Reset local agent database: `npm run reset-agent-db`
- Check Firestore security rules
- Verify Firebase configuration

### Build Issues
- Clear Next.js cache: `rm -rf .next`
- Check TypeScript errors: `npm run typecheck`
- Verify all dependencies are installed

## Contributing Guidelines

### Code Review Process
1. Create feature branch from main
2. Implement changes with tests
3. Ensure all checks pass
4. Submit pull request with clear description
5. Address review feedback

### Commit Convention
- Use conventional commits format
- Include scope when appropriate: `feat(ai): add new flow`
- Write clear, descriptive messages

### Documentation
- Update relevant documentation with changes
- Include JSDoc comments for complex functions
- Update type definitions when needed

### Code Cleaning Checklist
When cleaning code in any folder, ensure:
- Remove unused imports
- Fix ESLint warnings
- Improve code formatting
- Optimize imports
- Remove dead code

## Resources

### External Documentation
- [Next.js 15 Documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs)
- [Google Genkit Documentation](https://firebase.google.com/docs/genkit)
- [Firebase Documentation](https://firebase.google.com/docs)
- [Radix UI Documentation](https://radix-ui.com)
- [Tailwind CSS Documentation](https://tailwindcss.com/docs)

### Project-Specific Resources
- `memory-bank/` - Project context and documentation
- `docs/` - Additional project documentation
- `.rovodev/subagents/` - AI agent configurations
